elements.section: Manage as severe dehydration and refer urgently:
elements.text: Insert 2 large bore IV lines, if possible.

elements.section: Manage as severe dehydration and refer urgently:
elements.text: Give Ringer's lactate IV fluid as first fluid choice. If unavailable, give sodium chloride 0.9% IV:

elements.section: Manage as severe dehydration and refer urgently:
elements.text: Give 30mL/kg IV over first 30 minutes, then give 70mL/kg over next 2.5 hours, while awaiting transfer.

elements.section: Manage as severe dehydration and refer urgently:
elements.text: If transport delayed > 3 hours: continue 5mL/kg/hour IV.

elements.section: Manage as severe dehydration and refer urgently:
elements.text: If unable to insert IV line and patient able to drink, give oral rehydration solution (ORS) 30mL/kg over first 30 minutes, then 70mL/ kg over next 2.5 hours.

elements.section: Manage as severe dehydration and refer urgently:
elements.text: If unable to insert IV line and decreased level of consciousness, insert nasogastric tube (NGT) and give ORS 30mL/kg over first 30 minutes, then 70mL/kg over next 2.5 hours.

elements.section: Manage as severe dehydration and refer urgently:
elements.text: Calculate further fluids according to ongoing losses. Add 10mL/kg of IV fluid/ORS for every episode of diarrhoea or vomiting. Increase rate of fluids to give new total volume over the 2.5 hours1.
Reassess every 15-30 minutes.
If no better or worse, discuss with referral centre.
If awake, able to drink and pulse < 100, continue IV fluids, but also manage as some dehydration: give ORS 75mL/kg (or at least 2-4L) over 4 hours.
Manage as severe dehydration and refer urgently (see adjacent).

• If patient has watery diarrhoea (with or without vomiting) and has been in cholera outbreak area in past 5 days, cholera likely. Discuss all suspected cases of cholera with doctor. • If possible, isolate patient. Health worker to wear gloves and apron while attending to patient. Disinfect surfaces contaminated with secretions with 70% alcohol or chlorine-based disinfectant. • Check fingerprick glucose: if < 3 (< 4 if diabetes) 19. • Record each episode of diarrhoea and vomiting and use this to calculate ongoing losses when giving fluid replacement below.
